import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Ropelength and crossing number: the constant in $L(K) \geq a \operatorname{Cr}(K)^{3/4}$

The *ropelength* of a closed curve $C \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$ is $\operatorname{Len}(C) / \tau(C)$,
where $\operatorname{Len}(C)$ is its length and $\tau(C)$ is its *thickness*, the radius of the
largest embedded normal tube around $C$. The (minimum) ropelength $L(K)$ of a knot type $K$ is the
infimum of the ropelength over all curves realising $K$. Buck and Simon proved that
$L(K) \geq (4\pi/11)^{3/4} \operatorname{Cr}(K)^{3/4} \approx 1.105 \operatorname{Cr}(K)^{3/4}$
for every knot $K$, where $\operatorname{Cr}(K)$ is the crossing number. Computer tightenings of
torus knots suggest that the optimal constant cannot exceed $10.76$. Wikipedia's list of unsolved
problems asks:

"What constant $1.1 < a \leq 10.76$ governs the lower bound of a closed knot $K$'s minimum
ropelength $L(K) \geq a \operatorname{Cr}(K)^{3/4}$?"

Here a *knot* is a simple closed curve in $\mathbb{R}^3$, i.e. a topological embedding
`γ : Circle → ℝ³`, and two knots have the same *knot type* if their images are ambient
isotopic. Thickness is measured as a *radius* (as in Cantarella–Kusner–Sullivan and
Klotz–Maldonado), which is the convention in which the constants $1.1$ and $10.76$ are stated;
in this convention the round unit circle has ropelength $2\pi$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Ropelength](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ropelength)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [BS99] Buck, G., Simon, J., *Thickness and crossing number of knots*, Topology Appl. 91 (1999),
  245–257.
- [CKS02] Cantarella, J., Kusner, R. B., Sullivan, J. M., *On the minimum ropelength of knots and
  links*, Invent. Math. 150 (2002), 257–286.
  [arXiv:math/0103224](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0103224)
- [KM21] Klotz, A. R., Maldonado, M., *The ropelength of complex knots*, J. Phys. A 54 (2021).
  [arXiv:2108.01857](https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.01857)
- [KT25] Klotz, A. R., Thompson, F., *Ropelength-minimizing concentric helices and non-alternating
  torus knots*. [arXiv:2504.00861](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.00861)
-/

blocks.docstring:
Two subsets `K₁ K₂` of `ℝ³` are **ambient isotopic** if there is a continuous family
`H t`, `t ∈ [0, 1]`, of homeomorphisms of `ℝ³` with `H 0 = id` and `H 1 '' K₁ = K₂`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: ContinuousMap.Homotopy / Homeomorph (Mathlib has homotopies of maps but no ambient isotopy through homeomorphisms; searched `rg Isotopy`).
justification.name: WhatConstant11ALeq1076GovernsTheLowerBoundOfAClosedKnotK.AmbientIsotopic
justification.why_needed: Knot type (ambient isotopy of subsets of ℝ³) is needed to define minimum ropelength and crossing number as knot invariants; Mathlib has no isotopy notion.

blocks.name: AmbientIsotopic
blocks.text:
/-- Two subsets `K₁ K₂` of `ℝ³` are **ambient isotopic** if there is a continuous family
`H t`, `t ∈ [0, 1]`, of homeomorphisms of `ℝ³` with `H 0 = id` and `H 1 '' K₁ = K₂`. -/
def AmbientIsotopic (K₁ K₂ : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∃ H : I → ℝ³ ≃ₜ ℝ³, Continuous (fun p : I × ℝ³ => H p.1 p.2) ∧
    H 0 = Homeomorph.refl ℝ³ ∧ H 1 '' K₁ = K₂

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 57]
theorem AmbientIsotopic.refl (K : Set ℝ³) : AmbientIsotopic K K :=
  ⟨fun _ => Homeomorph.refl ℝ³, continuous_snd, rfl, by simp⟩
blocks.docstring: Every set is ambient isotopic to itself (via the constant isotopy).
blocks.name: AmbientIsotopic.refl
blocks.text:
/-- Every set is ambient isotopic to itself (via the constant isotopy). -/

theorem AmbientIsotopic.refl (K : Set ℝ³) : AmbientIsotopic K K :=

blocks.code:
noncomputable def thickness (K : Set ℝ³) : ℝ :=
  sInf {r | ∃ s : Affine.Simplex ℝ ℝ³ 2, (∀ i, s.points i ∈ K) ∧ s.circumradius = r}
blocks.docstring:
The **thickness** of a set `K ⊆ ℝ³`, following Gonzalez–Maddocks and [CKS02, §1]: the
infimum of the circumradii $r(x, y, z)$ over all triples of distinct points $x, y, z \in K$.
Collinear triples have $r = \infty$ and are omitted (they never contribute to the infimum). For a
`C¹` curve this equals the normal injectivity radius, i.e. the radius of the largest embedded
normal tube around the curve [CKS02, §1]; it is `0` for curves that are not `C^{1,1}`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Affine.Simplex.circumradius (used as the building block); Metric.infDist for a Federer-reach formulation (rejected as further from the cited source).
justification.name: WhatConstant11ALeq1076GovernsTheLowerBoundOfAClosedKnotK.thickness
justification.why_needed: Gonzalez–Maddocks thickness (infimum of circumradii of triangles inscribed in the curve) is the standard definition used by CKS; no notion of thickness, reach, or normal injectivity radius exists in Mathlib.

blocks.name: thickness
blocks.text:
/-- The **thickness** of a set `K ⊆ ℝ³`, following Gonzalez–Maddocks and [CKS02, §1]: the
infimum of the circumradii $r(x, y, z)$ over all triples of distinct points $x, y, z \in K$.
Collinear triples have $r = \infty$ and are omitted (they never contribute to the infimum). For a
`C¹` curve this equals the normal injectivity radius, i.e. the radius of the largest embedded
normal tube around the curve [CKS02, §1]; it is `0` for curves that are not `C^{1,1}`. -/
noncomputable def thickness (K : Set ℝ³) : ℝ :=
  sInf {r | ∃ s : Affine.Simplex ℝ ℝ³ 2, (∀ i, s.points i ∈ K) ∧ s.circumradius = r}

blocks.code:
noncomputable def ropelength (K : Set ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  μH[1] K / ENNReal.ofReal (thickness K)
blocks.docstring:
The **ropelength** of a set `K ⊆ ℝ³` (the image of a closed curve): its length, i.e. its
one-dimensional Hausdorff measure `μH[1] K`, divided by its thickness. It is `∞` when the curve
has zero thickness (and positive length) or infinite length.

justification.closest_existing_considered: MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure (μH[1], used for length); eVariationOn (alternative length notion, not image-based).
justification.name: WhatConstant11ALeq1076GovernsTheLowerBoundOfAClosedKnotK.ropelength
justification.why_needed: Ropelength = length / thickness of a curve; not in Mathlib.

blocks.name: ropelength
blocks.text:
/-- The **ropelength** of a set `K ⊆ ℝ³` (the image of a closed curve): its length, i.e. its
one-dimensional Hausdorff measure `μH[1] K`, divided by its thickness. It is `∞` when the curve
has zero thickness (and positive length) or infinite length. -/
noncomputable def ropelength (K : Set ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  μH[1] K / ENNReal.ofReal (thickness K)

blocks.code:
noncomputable def minRopelength (γ : Circle → ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨅ (γ' : Circle → ℝ³)
    (_ : IsEmbedding γ' ∧ AmbientIsotopic (Set.range γ) (Set.range γ')),
    ropelength (Set.range γ')
blocks.docstring:

blocks.code:
def crossingSet (γ : Circle → ℝ³) : Set (ℝ × ℝ) :=
  {p | (Set.range γ ∩ planeProj ⁻¹' {p}).encard = 2}
blocks.docstring:
The **crossings** of the vertical projection of `γ : Circle → ℝ³`: the points of the plane
with exactly two preimages on the curve.

justification.name: WhatConstant11ALeq1076GovernsTheLowerBoundOfAClosedKnotK.crossingSet
justification.why_needed: Set of double points of the vertical projection of a curve.

blocks.name: crossingSet

blocks.code:
structure IsRegularDiagram (γ : Circle → ℝ³) : Prop where
  contDiff : ContDiff ℝ 1 (periodicParam γ)
  immersion : ∀ t, deriv (planeProj ∘ periodicParam γ) t ≠ 0
  encard_le_two : ∀ p, (Set.range γ ∩ planeProj ⁻¹' {p}).encard ≤ 2
  finite : (crossingSet γ).Finite
  transverse : ∀ t₁ t₂, periodicParam γ t₁ ≠ periodicParam γ t₂ →
    planeProj (periodicParam γ t₁) = planeProj (periodicParam γ t₂) →
    LinearIndependent ℝ
      ![deriv (planeProj ∘ periodicParam γ) t₁, deriv (planeProj ∘ periodicParam γ) t₂]
blocks.docstring:
The curve `γ : Circle → ℝ³` is `C¹` and its vertical projection to the plane is a
**regular diagram**: the projected curve is an immersion, every point of the plane has at most
two preimages on the curve, there are finitely many double points, and at every double point
the two strands cross transversally.

justification.name: WhatConstant11ALeq1076GovernsTheLowerBoundOfAClosedKnotK.IsRegularDiagram
justification.why_needed: Regular projection of a C¹ knot (immersion, at most double points, finitely many, transverse); needed to define crossing number.

blocks.name: IsRegularDiagram
blocks.text:
/-- The curve `γ : Circle → ℝ³` is `C¹` and its vertical projection to the plane is a
**regular diagram**: the projected curve is an immersion, every point of the plane has at most
two preimages on the curve, there are finitely many double points, and at every double point
the two strands cross transversally. -/
structure IsRegularDiagram (γ : Circle → ℝ³) : Prop where
  contDiff : ContDiff ℝ 1 (periodicParam γ)
  immersion : ∀ t, deriv (planeProj ∘ periodicParam γ) t ≠ 0
  encard_le_two : ∀ p, (Set.range γ ∩ planeProj ⁻¹' {p}).encard ≤ 2
  finite : (crossingSet γ).Finite
  transverse : ∀ t₁ t₂, periodicParam γ t₁ ≠ periodicParam γ t₂ →
    planeProj (periodicParam γ t₁) = planeProj (periodicParam γ t₂) →
    LinearIndependent ℝ
      ![deriv (planeProj ∘ periodicParam γ) t₁, deriv (planeProj ∘ periodicParam γ) t₂]

blocks.code:
noncomputable def crossingNumber (γ : Circle → ℝ³) : ℕ :=
  sInf {n | ∃ γ' : Circle → ℝ³,
    IsEmbedding γ' ∧ AmbientIsotopic (Set.range γ) (Set.range γ') ∧
    IsRegularDiagram γ' ∧ (crossingSet γ').ncard = n}
blocks.docstring:
The **crossing number** of the knot type of the knot `γ`: the least number of crossings in a
regular diagram of a knot `γ'` whose image is ambient isotopic to that of `γ`. (Any regular
projection direction can be rotated to the vertical one by an ambient isotopy, so it suffices to
consider vertical projections.) For a knot type with no `C¹` representative (a wild knot) the set
below is empty and the value is `0`; such knot types have infinite ropelength.

justification.closest_existing_considered: None in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib (searched `rg -i knot|crossing`).
justification.name: WhatConstant11ALeq1076GovernsTheLowerBoundOfAClosedKnotK.crossingNumber
justification.why_needed: Crossing number Cr(K) of a knot type, the other quantity in the statement.

blocks.name: crossingNumber
blocks.text:
/-- The **crossing number** of the knot type of the knot `γ`: the least number of crossings in a
regular diagram of a knot `γ'` whose image is ambient isotopic to that of `γ`. (Any regular
projection direction can be rotated to the vertical one by an ambient isotopy, so it suffices to
consider vertical projections.) For a knot type with no `C¹` representative (a wild knot) the set
below is empty and the value is `0`; such knot types have infinite ropelength. -/
noncomputable def crossingNumber (γ : Circle → ℝ³) : ℕ :=
  sInf {n | ∃ γ' : Circle → ℝ³,
    IsEmbedding γ' ∧ AmbientIsotopic (Set.range γ) (Set.range γ') ∧
    IsRegularDiagram γ' ∧ (crossingSet γ').ncard = n}

blocks.docstring:
The optimal constant `a` in the lower bound $L(K) \geq a \operatorname{Cr}(K)^{3/4}$: the
supremum of all `a : ℝ` such that `a * Cr(K) ^ (3/4) ≤ L(K)` holds for every knot type `K`,
where `L(K)` is the minimum ropelength and `Cr(K)` the crossing number of `K`. The unknot has
`Cr = 0` and imposes no constraint, so this is the infimum of $L(K) / \operatorname{Cr}(K)^{3/4}$
over all nontrivial knots.

justification.name: WhatConstant11ALeq1076GovernsTheLowerBoundOfAClosedKnotK.ropelengthCrossingConstant
justification.why_needed: The optimal constant a* asked about in the statement.

blocks.name: ropelengthCrossingConstant
blocks.text:
/-- The optimal constant `a` in the lower bound $L(K) \geq a \operatorname{Cr}(K)^{3/4}$: the
supremum of all `a : ℝ` such that `a * Cr(K) ^ (3/4) ≤ L(K)` holds for every knot type `K`,
where `L(K)` is the minimum ropelength and `Cr(K)` the crossing number of `K`. The unknot has
`Cr = 0` and imposes no constraint, so this is the infimum of $L(K) / \operatorname{Cr}(K)^{3/4}$
over all nontrivial knots. -/
noncomputable def ropelengthCrossingConstant : ℝ :=
  sSup {a : ℝ | ∀ γ : Circle → ℝ³, IsEmbedding γ →
    ENNReal.ofReal (a * (crossingNumber γ : ℝ) ^ (3 / 4 : ℝ)) ≤ minRopelength γ}

blocks.docstring:
**Ropelength versus crossing number.**
Let $a^*$ be the optimal constant such that every closed knot $K$ satisfies
$L(K) \geq a^* \operatorname{Cr}(K)^{3/4}$, where $L(K)$ is the minimum ropelength and
$\operatorname{Cr}(K)$ the crossing number of $K$. Then $1.1 < a^* \leq 10.76$.

The lower bound is the theorem of Buck and Simon [BS99] (see also [CKS02, §10]), which gives
$a^* \geq (4\pi/11)^{3/4} \approx 1.105$. The upper bound rests on computer tightenings of
$T(Q+1, Q)$ torus knots with at least $224$ crossings [KM21], [KT25], and is not proven.

claims.decomposer_note: Asks for the exact value of the optimal constant a* = inf over nontrivial knots K of L(K)/Cr(K)^{3/4} (ropelength in radius units, thickness 1; the unknot with Cr = 0 must be excluded from the infimum); the article says the constant 'is not known exactly' and the only number floated in the sources (8.65, Klotz–Maldonado) is explicitly a heuristic that the authors 'do not assert' is the true prefactor, so no candidate answer exists and there is no Prop to state.

claims.decomposer_note: The stated range for the optimal constant a* (sup of all a with L(K) ≥ a·Cr(K)^{3/4} for every knot K, equivalently the infimum of L(K)/Cr(K)^{3/4} over nontrivial knots) is a single Prop 1.1 < a* ∧ a* ≤ 10.76; the lower half is Buck–Simon's proven (4π/11)^{3/4} ≈ 1.105, while the upper half (existence of a knot, numerically a T(Q+1,Q) torus knot with ≥ 224 crossings, with L(K) ≤ 10.76·Cr(K)^{3/4}) rests only on computer tightening and is not proven, so a formalizer may wish to split the two halves into separate declarations with different categories; the statement restricts to knots (not links), consistent with the 10.76 witness being a knot.
claims.reviewer_why: c04 is the most faithful of the five compiled files: knots are arbitrary topological embeddings Circle → ℝ³ (so 'minimum ropelength over all curves realising K' is taken literally, as in Wikipedia/CKS), knot type is genuine ambient isotopy (continuous family of homeomorphisms starting at id), thickness is exactly the Gonzalez–Maddocks/CKS infimum of circumradii over non-collinear triples (radius convention, in which both 1.1 ≈ (4π/11)^{3/4} and 10.76 are stated), length is μH[1] of the image, ropelength is ℝ≥0∞-valued so zero-thickness/wild curves get ⊤ instead of x/0 = 0 junk, and crossing number is the textbook regular-diagram minimum (C¹, immersed projection, ≤2 preimages, finitely many transverse double points). The optimal constant is sSup of the downward-closed set {a | ∀ knots, ofReal(a·Cr^{3/4}) ≤ L}, which contains all a ≤ 0 and is bounded above by the trefoil ratio, so no Real.sSup junk; Cr(unknot)=0 gives 0^{3/4}=0 and no constraint, matching the 'inf over nontrivial knots' reading. Edits: removed the `.variants.value` answer(sorry) declaration (the question form is in the Dropped list), corrected the arXiv:2504.00861 authors (Klotz–Thompson) and the CKS section reference (§10), and added four `category test` statements for the round unit circle (embedding, thickness 1, ropelength 2π, crossing number 0) that pin down the radius convention. c05 (C¹ regular curves, ENNReal thickness, all linear projections) and c07 (set-based, crossing number without transversality) are also essentially correct but rely on extra equivalence arguments (positive thickness ⇒ C^{1,1}; taming of planar graphs); c01 uses Federer reach and real division; c06 identifies mirror images via arbitrary homeomorphisms and uses real division. c02/c03/c08 bailed on missing primitives, but the bespoke definitions here are standard and small enough to be faithful, so the bail-outs are not persuasive.

context:
In physical knot theory, each realization of a link or knot has an associated ropelength. Intuitively this is the minimal length of an ideally flexible rope that is needed to tie a given link, or knot. Knots and links that minimize ropelength are called ideal knots and ideal links respectively.
The ropelength problem is open: neither for knots nor for open knots in a long rope has an expression been found (in 2026) that describes the ropelength of tight, ideal knots. The problem is unsolved (as of 2026) for every non-trivial knot.

decomposition_objections.text: None. /-!
# Ropelength and crossing number: the constant in $L(K) \geq a \operatorname{Cr}(K)^{3/4}$

The *ropelength* of a closed curve $C \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$ is $\operatorname{Len}(C) / \tau(C)$,
where $\operatorname{Len}(C)$ is its length and $\tau(C)$ is its *thickness*, the radius of the
largest embedded normal tube around $C$. The (minimum) ropelength $L(K)$ of a knot type $K$ is the
infimum of the ropelength over all curves realising $K$. Buck and Simon proved that
$L(K) \geq (4\pi/11)^{3/4} \operatorname{Cr}(K)^{3/4} \approx 1.105 \operatorname{Cr}(K)^{3/4}$
for every knot $K$, where $\operatorname{Cr}(K)$ is the crossing number. Computer tightenings of
torus knots suggest that the optimal constant cannot exceed $10.76$. Wikipedia's list of unsolved
problems asks:

"What constant $1.1 < a \leq 10.76$ governs the lower bound of a closed knot $K$'s minimum
ropelength $L(K) \geq a \operatorname{Cr}(K)^{3/4}$?"

Here a *knot* is a simple closed curve in $\mathbb{R}^3$, i.e. a topological embedding
`γ : Circle → ℝ³`, and two knots have the same *knot type* if their images are ambient
isotopic. Thickness is measured as a *radius* (as in Cantarella–Kusner–Sullivan and
Klotz–Maldonado), which is the convention in which the constants $1.1$ and $10.76$ are stated;
in this convention the round unit circle has ropelength $2\pi$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Ropelength](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ropelength)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [BS99] Buck, G., Simon, J., *Thickness and crossing number of knots*, Topology Appl. 91 (1999),
  245–257.
- [CKS02] Cantarella, J., Kusner, R. B., Sullivan, J. M., *On the minimum ropelength of knots and
  links*, Invent. Math. 150 (2002), 257–286.
  [arXiv:math/0103224](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0103224)
- [KM21] Klotz, A. R., Maldonado, M., *The ropelength of complex knots*, J. Phys. A 54 (2021).
  [arXiv:2108.01857](https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.01857)
- [KT25] Klotz, A. R., Thompson, F., *Ropelength-minimizing concentric helices and non-alternating
  torus knots*. [arXiv:2504.00861](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.00861)
-/

namespace WhatConstant11ALeq1076GovernsTheLowerBoundOfAClosedKnotK

open Topology
open scoped EuclideanGeometry MeasureTheory ENNReal Real unitInterval

/-- Two subsets `K₁ K₂` of `ℝ³` are **ambient isotopic** if there is a continuous family
`H t`, `t ∈ [0, 1]`, of homeomorphisms of `ℝ³` with `H 0 = id` and `H 1 '' K₁ = K₂`. -/
def AmbientIsotopic (K₁ K₂ : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∃ H : I → ℝ³ ≃ₜ ℝ³, Continuous (fun p : I × ℝ³ => H p.1 p.2) ∧
    H 0 = Homeomorph.refl ℝ³ ∧ H 1 '' K₁ = K₂

/-- Every set is ambient isotopic to itself (via the constant isotopy). -/
@[category API, AMS 57]
theorem AmbientIsotopic.refl (K : Set ℝ³) : AmbientIsotopic K K :=
  ⟨fun _ => Homeomorph.refl ℝ³, continuous_snd, rfl, by simp⟩

/-- The **thickness** of a set `K ⊆ ℝ³`, following Gonzalez–Maddocks and [CKS02, §1]: the
infimum of the circumradii $r(x, y, z)$ over all triples of distinct points $x, y, z \in K$.
Collinear triples have $r = \infty$ and are omitted (they never contribute to the infimum). For a
`C¹` curve this equals the normal injectivity radius, i.e. the radius of the largest embedded
normal tube around the curve [CKS02, §1]; it is `0` for curves that are not `C^{1,1}`. -/
noncomputable def thickness (K : Set ℝ³) : ℝ :=
  sInf {r | ∃ s : Affine.Simplex ℝ ℝ³ 2, (∀ i, s.points i ∈ K) ∧ s.circumradius = r}

/-- The **ropelength** of a set `K ⊆ ℝ³` (the image of a closed curve): its length, i.e. its
one-dimensional Hausdorff measure `μH[1] K`, divided by its thickness. It is `∞` when the curve
has zero thickness (and positive length) or infinite length. -/
noncomputable def ropelength (K : Set ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  μH[1] K / ENNReal.ofReal (thickness K)

/-- The **minimum ropelength** of the knot type of the knot `γ`: the infimum of the ropelength
over all knots `γ'` whose image is ambient isotopic to that of `γ`. -/
noncomputable def minRopelength (γ : Circle → ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨅ (γ' : Circle → ℝ³)
    (_ : IsEmbedding γ' ∧ AmbientIsotopic (Set.range γ) (Set.range γ')),
    ropelength (Set.range γ')

/-- The vertical projection `ℝ³ → ℝ × ℝ` onto the first two coordinates. -/
def planeProj (p : ℝ³) : ℝ × ℝ := (p 0, p 1)

/-- The `2π`-periodic parametrisation `t ↦ γ (Circle.exp t)` of a curve
`γ : Circle → ℝ³`. -/
noncomputable def periodicParam (γ : Circle → ℝ³) : ℝ → ℝ³ :=
  fun t => γ (Circle.exp t)

/-- The **crossings** of the vertical projection of `γ : Circle → ℝ³`: the points of the plane
with exactly two preimages on the curve. -/
def crossingSet (γ : Circle → ℝ³) : Set (ℝ × ℝ) :=
  {p | (Set.range γ ∩ planeProj ⁻¹' {p}).encard = 2}

/-- The curve `γ : Circle → ℝ³` is `C¹` and its vertical projection to the plane is a
**regular diagram**: the projected curve is an immersion, every point of the plane has at most
two preimages on the curve, there are finitely many double points, and at every double point
the two strands cross transversally. -/
structure IsRegularDiagram (γ : Circle → ℝ³) : Prop where
  contDiff : ContDiff ℝ 1 (periodicParam γ)
  immersion : ∀ t, deriv (planeProj ∘ periodicParam γ) t ≠ 0
  encard_le_two : ∀ p, (Set.range γ ∩ planeProj ⁻¹' {p}).encard ≤ 2
  finite : (crossingSet γ).Finite
  transverse : ∀ t₁ t₂, periodicParam γ t₁ ≠ periodicParam γ t₂ →
    planeProj (periodicParam γ t₁) = planeProj (periodicParam γ t₂) →
    LinearIndependent ℝ
      ![deriv (planeProj ∘ periodicParam γ) t₁, deriv (planeProj ∘ periodicParam γ) t₂]

/-- The **crossing number** of the knot type of the knot `γ`: the least number of crossings in a
regular diagram of a knot `γ'` whose image is ambient isotopic to that of `γ`. (Any regular
projection direction can be rotated to the vertical one by an ambient isotopy, so it suffices to
consider vertical projections.) For a knot type with no `C¹` representative (a wild knot) the set
below is empty and the value is `0`; such knot types have infinite ropelength. -/
noncomputable def crossingNumber (γ : Circle → ℝ³) : ℕ :=
  sInf {n | ∃ γ' : Circle → ℝ³,
    IsEmbedding γ' ∧ AmbientIsotopic (Set.range γ) (Set.range γ') ∧
    IsRegularDiagram γ' ∧ (crossingSet γ').ncard = n}

/-- The optimal constant `a` in the lower bound $L(K) \geq a \operatorname{Cr}(K)^{3/4}$: the
supremum of all `a : ℝ` such that `a * Cr(K) ^ (3/4) ≤ L(K)` holds for every knot type `K`,
where `L(K)` is the minimum ropelength and `Cr(K)` the crossing number of `K`. The unknot has
`Cr = 0` and imposes no constraint, so this is the infimum of $L(K) / \operatorname{Cr}(K)^{3/4}$
over all nontrivial knots. -/
noncomputable def ropelengthCrossingConstant : ℝ :=
  sSup {a : ℝ | ∀ γ : Circle → ℝ³, IsEmbedding γ →
    ENNReal.ofReal (a * (crossingNumber γ : ℝ) ^ (3 / 4 : ℝ)) ≤ minRopelength γ}

/-- The round unit circle in the plane $x_2 = 0$. -/
noncomputable def roundCircle : Circle → ℝ³ :=
  fun z => !₂[(z : ℂ).re, (z : ℂ).im, 0]

@[category test, AMS 51 57]
theorem isEmbedding_roundCircle : IsEmbedding roundCircle := by
  sorry

/-- Every non-degenerate triangle inscribed in the unit circle has circumradius `1`. -/
@[category test, AMS 51 57]
theorem thickness_range_roundCircle : thickness (Set.range roundCircle) = 1 := by
  sorry

/-- The round unit circle has length `2π` and thickness `1`, so its ropelength is `2π`. -/
@[category test, AMS 51 57]
theorem ropelength_range_roundCircle :
    ropelength (Set.range roundCircle) = ENNReal.ofReal (2 * π) := by
  sorry

/-- The vertical projection of the round circle is injective, so the unknot has crossing
number `0`. -/
@[category test, AMS 51 57]
theorem crossingNumber_roundCircle : crossingNumber roundCircle = 0 := by
  sorry

/--
**Ropelength versus crossing number.**
Let $a^*$ be the optimal constant such that every closed knot $K$ satisfies
$L(K) \geq a^* \operatorname{Cr}(K)^{3/4}$, where $L(K)$ is the minimum ropelength and
$\operatorname{Cr}(K)$ the crossing number of $K$. Then $1.1 < a^* \leq 10.76$.

The lower bound is the theorem of Buck and Simon [BS99] (see also [CKS02, §10]), which gives
$a^* \geq (4\pi/11)^{3/4} \approx 1.105$. The upper bound rests on computer tightenings of
$T(Q+1, Q)$ torus knots with at least $224$ crossings [KM21], [KT25], and is not proven.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51 57]
theorem what_constant_1_1_a_leq_10_76_governs_the_lower_bound_of_a_closed_knot_k :
    1.1 < ropelengthCrossingConstant ∧ ropelengthCrossingConstant ≤ 10.76 := by
  sorry

/-- The lower half: the optimal constant exceeds $1.1$. This follows from the theorem of
Buck and Simon [BS99], since $(4\pi/11)^{3/4} > 1.1$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 51 57]
theorem what_constant_1_1_a_leq_10_76_governs_the_lower_bound_of_a_closed_knot_k.variants.lower_bound :
    1.1 < ropelengthCrossingConstant := by
  sorry

/-- The theorem of Buck and Simon [BS99], as stated in [CKS02, §10]: every knot type $K$ satisfies
$L(K) \geq (4\pi \operatorname{Cr}(K) / 11)^{3/4}$; hence $a^* \geq (4\pi/11)^{3/4}$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 51 57]
theorem what_constant_1_1_a_leq_10_76_governs_the_lower_bound_of_a_closed_knot_k.variants.buck_simon :
    (4 * π / 11) ^ (3 / 4 : ℝ) ≤ ropelengthCrossingConstant := by
  sorry

/-- The upper half: the optimal constant is at most $10.76$, i.e. for every $a > 10.76$ some
knot $K$ has $L(K) < a \operatorname{Cr}(K)^{3/4}$. This is supported by computer tightenings of
torus knots [KM21], [KT25], but is not proven. -/
@[category research open, AMS 51 57]
theorem what_constant_1_1_a_leq_10_76_governs_the_lower_bound_of_a_closed_knot_k.variants.upper_bound :
    ropelengthCrossingConstant ≤ 10.76 := by
  sorry

end WhatConstant11ALeq1076GovernsTheLowerBoundOfAClosedKnotK

items: Convention: thickness is the RADIUS of the largest embedded normal tube (Gonzalez–Maddocks / Cantarella–Kusner–Sullivan / Klotz–Maldonado convention). This is the convention in which both constants of the statement live: (4π/11)^{3/4} ≈ 1.105 (CKS §5 citing Buck–Simon, radius convention) and 10.76 (Klotz–Maldonado, unit-radius tubes). Note the Wikipedia article's other numbers (15.66, 16.372) are in the diameter convention; in that convention the constants would be halved.

The unknown constant a* is defined as sSup {a : ℝ | ∀ knot γ, ofReal(a·Cr(γ)^{3/4}) ≤ minRopelength γ}. This set contains all a ≤ 0 and is bounded above (any smooth trefoil has finite ropelength and Cr = 3), so sSup is the genuine supremum; it equals the infimum of L(K)/Cr(K)^{3/4} over nontrivial knots (the unknot, Cr = 0, imposes no constraint), matching the decomposition note.

Knots are topological embeddings γ : Circle → ℝ³ (as in Wikipedia/InscribedSquare.lean); knot type = ambient isotopy of the image sets, via a continuous family H : I → (ℝ³ ≃ₜ ℝ³) with H 0 = id and H 1 '' K₁ = K₂. Knots only (no links), unoriented; mirror images are distinct types but have the same L and Cr so this is immaterial.

Thickness of a set K is the Gonzalez–Maddocks global radius of curvature: sInf of circumradii (`Affine.Simplex.circumradius`) of all non-degenerate triangles with vertices in K. Collinear triples (r = ∞ in GM) are omitted; for a simple closed curve non-collinear triples always exist, so sInf is the true infimum. By CKS this equals the normal injectivity radius for C¹ curves and is 0 for curves that are not C^{1,1}.

Length of a curve is taken as the 1-dimensional Hausdorff measure μH[1] of its image (equals arc length for simple curves; Mathlib's normalisation gives length for segments). Ropelength is ℝ≥0∞-valued: μH[1] K / ENNReal.ofReal (thickness K); for zero thickness and positive length this is ⊤ (`ENNReal.div_zero`), which is the intended value. Minimum ropelength of a type is the ⨅ over embeddings isotopic to the given one (includes the knot itself, so never an empty infimum).

Crossing number of the type of γ: sInf over ℕ of the number of double points of a regular vertical projection of a C¹ knot γ' isotopic to γ. Regular = projection is an immersion (deriv ≠ 0), every point of the plane has ≤ 2 preimages on the curve, finitely many double points, and transversality (linearly independent tangents) at each double point. Projection direction is fixed to the vertical since any direction can be rotated to it by an ambient isotopy. C¹ smoothness is expressed via the 2π-periodic lift t ↦ γ (Circle.exp t). For wild knot types (no C¹ representative) the set is empty and Cr = 0, which is harmless: such types have thickness 0 for all realisations, hence L = ⊤, and the inequality is trivial.
Real.rpow with exponent (3/4 : ℝ) is used; 0^(3/4) = 0 so Cr = 0 gives no constraint, as intended.

Variants added: `.variants.lower_bound` (1.1 < a*, research solved, Buck–Simon), `.variants.buck_simon` ((4π/11)^{3/4} ≤ a*, research solved, as stated in CKS §5 with the radius convention), `.variants.upper_bound` (a* ≤ 10.76, research open — rests on computer tightenings), `.variants.value` (a* = answer(sorry), the literal 'what constant' question). Reviewers should check the radius-convention reading of the Buck–Simon constant for the `buck_simon` variant.

reviewer_notes: Units: both constants are in the radius convention (CKS restates Buck–Simon as L ≥ (4πn/11)^{3/4} with thickness = tube radius; Klotz–Maldonado use unit-radius tubes; Wikipedia's 'proven to be above 1.1' only holds in radius units — in diameter units it would be ≈0.55). The final file follows this convention and records it via the test `ropelength (round unit circle) = 2π`. Per the decomposition notes, the two halves are also split as variants: `variants.lower_bound` and `variants.buck_simon` are `research solved` (Buck–Simon 1999 via CKS §10); `variants.upper_bound` is `research open` (rests only on computer tightening of T(Q+1,Q) torus knots, KM21/KT25); the slot declaration itself is the conjunction, `research open`. The answer(sorry) form of the literal 'what constant' question was deliberately omitted (Dropped list). Non-obvious modelling facts a reviewer should be aware of: (i) wild knot types have every representative of thickness 0, hence L = ⊤, and Cr = sInf ∅ = 0 — no constraint either way; (ii) crossing number fixes the vertical projection, justified because rotations are ambient isotopies; (iii) μH[1] of an embedded circle equals its arc length under Mathlib's normalisation (μH[1] = volume on ℝ).
